identityReview: Sadiq Aman Khan, born 8 October 1970 in Tooting. Current Mayor of London and Labour life peer Lord Khan of Tooting; distinct from the City of London’s Lord Mayor and from other peers surnamed Khan. Former Commons MP 2005–2016, communities junior minister and transport minister of state, not transport secretary of state. 20 August 2026 creation of life barony and 15 September introduction/oath are distinct. Historical alumni errors do not override parliamentary dates.
lifeStatusEvidence: City Hall’s 13 November 2026 body explicitly reports his actual Istanbul Chamber of Commerce meeting that morning and subsequent activity. Tokyo’s 6 November joint communiqué independently records the prior meeting with Governor Koike in London. These are completed activities, rather than an undated profile or future itinerary.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read City Hall biography, archive authority record, law-school alumni page, current parliamentary career, official 2016/2024 election analyses and 2021/2024 results, actual ULEZ launch release, selected original 2025 evaluation sections, House of Lords introduction and Hansard, Tokyo–London communiqué and current Istanbul meeting account. Read Commons crop/parent history and refreshed official parliamentary portrait/licence page.
corrections: Read current City Hall profile, showing a mayoral term beginning May 2024, North London legal studies and Wandsworth councillor service 1994–2006. Its 2008 Minister of State for Communities wording conflicts with Parliament’s precise parliamentary-under-secretary record; the latter is used. Broad claims about personal mandates and pioneering status are not treated as audited rankings. Council and Commons service overlap rather than being artificially sequential.

Read Royal Albert Hall archive authority record DS/UK/21512: Sadiq Aman Khan, born 8 October 1970, Tooting, and North London law studies. The National’s separate biography corroborates date and birthplace. The authority record is not an original birth certificate; its ministerial shorthand and superlative mandate claims are not used over Parliament. Private family details are omitted.

Read University of Law alumni page, originally published in 2019: Guildford Law Society Finals in 1992–1993, predecessor to LPC, followed by legal work. The historical College of Law identity is used for that period. The page incorrectly truncates Commons tenure to 2005–2006; Parliament establishes 2005–2016. Its trainee/partner timeline is not used to resolve conflicting law-qualification and degree-completion years. The National says 1991 graduation whereas other legal profiles suggest 1992; exact undergraduate completion year is omitted.

Read parliamentary career: Commons 5 May 2005–9 May 2016, one election before 2010 boundary version and two afterwards; assistant whip 2 July 2007–5 October 2008; communities parliamentary under-secretary 5 October 2008–9 June 2009; transport minister of state 9 June 2009–6 May 2010. Shadow justice offices 8 October 2010–30 March 2015, shadow London 16 January 2013–30 March 2015. Current Labour Lords membership starts 20 August 2026. This is not current Commons, a secretary-of-state appointment or the City of London’s Lord Mayoralty.

Read Commons Library’s 2016 election analysis: polling 5 May, 1,148,716 first preferences and 1,310,143 after second-preference transfers. These counts concern different stages under supplementary voting. The profile uses polling day, not an asserted result-declaration or oath date, and does not compare the final transferable total directly with 2024 single-vote totals as a measure of identical support. Parliament independently provides the 9 May Commons departure.

Read London Elects 2024 official results factsheet: 13 mayoral candidates; first-past-the-post; Khan 1,088,225 and winner. Its result figures and voting-system description are used, not partisan summaries. The document says the count was manual and explains ward-level publication limits; no invented ward-level data or unsupported turnout calculation is added.

Read Commons Library’s 2024 analysis: election held 2 May, third mayoral term and 1,088,225 votes, rounded 44%. Polling date is distinct from later count/result announcements; 44% is not a majority of all London residents. No claim that Labour controlled every Assembly seat, or that the mayor alone determines all London policy, is made.

Read City Hall’s actual 8 April 2019 ULEZ launch release and its note on bringing the start forward. Launch is distinct from earlier proposals and approvals, so Khan is not called sole inventor of every low-emission policy. Emission standards, congestion charging and blanket bans are different. Its future forecasts for bus fleets, emissions and schools are not retrospectively labelled fulfilled. Historical launch settings are not assumed to be all current 2026 rules.

Read March 2025 GLA report’s executive summary, expansion chronology, selected air-quality results and Table 29, not the complete technical appendices. Expansion across all boroughs occurred 29 August 2023. Table 29 labels the 2024 concentration comparison as up to September; the 27% reduction is relative to a modelled no-ULEZ scenario for all phases, not a year-on-year measured fall, all pollutants, health outcomes, or the 2023 expansion alone. Rounded concentration cells are not used to recalculate the reported effect. Owner costs, exemptions and access to alternatives are distinct from the reported air metric; no blanket claim of zero cost or no individual economic loss is made.

Read House of Lords formal introduction record for 15 September 2026: life barony created by Letters Patent dated the afternoon of 20 August; introduction, oath and Code of Conduct undertaking recorded. Hansard separately confirms Sir Sadiq Aman Khan’s identity and the same ceremony. Creation date and first ceremonial participation are distinct. Life peerage is not hereditary, and he remains mayor according to current City Hall material.

Read Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s original 6 November 2026 joint communiqué: Koike and Khan met at London City Hall; AI, cybersecurity, climate and urban cooperation discussed. The extracted visual description of logos/names is not a claim of inspecting handwritten signatures or video. The meeting is actual; commitments do not establish completed AI systems, funding flows or quantified benefits.

Read City Hall’s 13 November 2026 report body: that morning’s Istanbul Chamber of Commerce business meeting, subsequent meetings and visits, following COP31 participation. It provides recent actual activity rather than just the 29 October trip announcement. The profile describes investment discussions, not signed contracts, realised investment, forecast 2050 rankings or a completed future free-trade agreement. No original event video was watched.

Read London Elects’ official 2021 results page naming Sadiq Aman Khan the elected mayor. This corroborates the intermediate re-election between 2016 and 2024. No exact polling, count or oath date is inferred from a page heading, and no 2021 vote total is needed in this biography.

Read historical biography corroborating 8 October 1970 Tooting birth. Its undergraduate completion year and ministerial chronology are not preferred over primary education and parliamentary records; unrelated counterterrorism/legal claims are not imported.

Read institutional explanation of separate Mayor of London and City Lord Mayor roles, updated 3 November 2026. No need to import the other officeholder’s identity or future term into Khan’s biography.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original birth certificate, final undergraduate degree-year reconciliation, complete ULEZ technical-appendix audit or independent causal reanalysis, full assessment of vehicle-owner burdens, original meeting video, portrait pixels or verified cached-file restoration. The 27% figure is an attributed official model estimate for the stated period. Forward investments, policy targets and trade negotiations remain distinct from realised outcomes.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed for Tooting birth, 1992–1993 Law Society Finals rather than invented graduate degree, councillor/Commons overlap, parliamentary-under-secretary and minister-of-state distinctions, 2016 first/second preference totals and 9 May Commons departure, 2021 re-election, 2024 first-past-the-post and 1,088,225 votes, 2019 ULEZ launch versus 2023 expansion, modelled 27% all-phase NO2 estimate through September 2024, 20 August life-peer creation versus 15 September 2026 oath, City Lord Mayor distinction and actual 6/13 November meetings.
